niche.diet: Sulfur, kaolin clay, arsenic, mercury, salt

chains.trait: Sulfur-secreting glands puffing white vapor near vents
links: Fumaroles emit sulfur gas and raw sulfur deposits
Sulfur is toxic to most but fuel for specialized metabolism
Glands evolve to store and secrete sulfur for defense
Sulfur coat deters predators and preserves skin

skill.effect: Sprays sulfur cloud; damages vision and stamina of attackers; ignites if near fire.

chains.weakness: Limited supply; must return to vents to recharge; smell reveals position.
observe: Glands along back puff white vapor when threatened.
Sight of sulfur makes nearby creatures gag or flee.
Creature licks raw sulfur crusts from rock.

journal.en: It wears the mountain's breath as a second skin.

plausibility.summary: Glands emit H₂S/SO₂-rich mist or fine sulfur powder from ingested crusts (recharge at fumaroles); reserve true combustion synergy for the flamethrower secret lineage on drought/fire years (F5, F15).
fixes: Glands emit H₂S/SO₂-rich mist or fine sulfur powder from ingested crusts (recharge at fumaroles); reserve true combustion synergy for the flamethrower secret lineage on drought/fire years (F5, F15).

analogues.organism: Bombardier beetle (Brachinus): exothermic quinone spray—not sulfur, but precedent for directed chemical defense; vent shrimp accumulate sulfur bacteria on carapace.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

chains.trait: Detox gut symbionts processing arsenic and mercury crusts
links: Hot springs contain arsenic and mercury poisons
Niche competition forces utilization of toxic resources
Symbiotic bacteria evolve to metabolize toxins
Sosa becomes immune to poisons that kill others

skill.effect: Immune to arsenic, mercury, and sulfur poisoning; can eat toxic food.

chains.weakness: Starves if toxic minerals are absent; vulnerable to non-toxic starvation.
observe: Eats bright orange arsenic crust without distress.
Gills do not flare; skin remains calm.
Other creatures avoid the crust; Sosa thrives.

journal.en: Poison is bread; the crust is its only home.

plausibility.summary: Arsenic: symbiont reduction + host thiol sequestration; mercury: bind and slowly shed in keratin/slime, not complete metabolism; starvation without licks stays.
fixes: Arsenic: symbiont reduction + host thiol sequestration; mercury: bind and slowly shed in keratin/slime, not complete metabolism; starvation without licks stays.

analogues.organism: Arsenic-tolerant microbes in Mono Lake–type habitats; parrots and macaws geophagy at clay licks (detox/adsorption, not full metal catabolism).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Heat-resistant keratin steaming on hot rock
links: Volcano slopes have high temperature near vents
Thermal stress damages cells and proteins
Heat shock proteins and thick keratin evolve for protection
Sosa can bask on hot rock to regulate metabolism

skill.effect: Immune to fire and heat damage; moves faster in volcanic zones.

chains.weakness: Overheats in direct sun or warm meadows; stamina drain.
observe: Walks on hot rock; skin steams slightly.
Active in steam vents; rests in heat.
No burns from contact with warm tuff.

journal.en: The stone is cool to its belly.

plausibility.summary: Passive resist = warm geothermal substrate and radiant heat near vents; stamina penalty in sunlit meadows (F15); full fire resist only via evolved flamethrower secret using dietary sulfur (F26).
fixes: Passive resist = warm geothermal substrate and radiant heat near vents; stamina penalty in sunlit meadows (F15); full fire resist only via evolved flamethrower secret using dietary sulfur (F26).

analogues.organism: Desert lizards on hot sand; alvinellid worms at vent gradients (much hotter—do not copy their limit); garden snail epiphragm keratin against desiccation, extended here for thermal shielding.

chains.trait: Gastrolith cache of basalt grit and kaolin clay
links: Mineral diet requires grinding for nutrient release
Lack of teeth or chewing surfaces necessitates grit
Stomach stones evolve for digestion and mineral intake
Grit also aids in detoxification by binding toxins

skill.effect: Reduces damage from bites; restores stamina when eating minerals.

chains.weakness: Heavy stomach slows movement; must regurgitate if overfed.
observe: Creature licks salt and clay licks.

journal.en: It eats the cliff to digest the world.

plausibility.summary: F23 basalt grit and kaolin align with canon mineral diet; gastroliths grind low-nutrient stone and clay; kaolin adsorbs alkaloids/toxins (pairs with poison immunity chain). Mass cost slowing a Babosa crawler is realistic.

relations.note: (council kind 'Mimicry') Coloso rests on volcano slopes; Sosa licks salt near Coloso's path. Coloso ignores Sosa unless provoked.
(council kind 'Deterrent') Espinodo avoids Sosa; Sosa's sulfur coat is toxic to Espinodo's sensitive nose and spine.

moments: Steam hisses from the hidden cave mouth; inside, a Sosa grinds its teeth on a hot rock, glowing faintly orange in the dark as sulfur vapors curl around its keratin shell.

journal.en: It eats poison and heat. The mountain feeds it, and it feeds the fire.
It holds the secret of the flame in its gut; sulfur and stone.
